Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Environment: Moderate temperatures (18–27°C), high humidity with poor air circulation. Unlike many fungal diseases, powdery mildew does not require free water on leaves.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Spread: Wind-borne fungal spores spread rapidly between plants and orchards.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Description: Powdery Mildew is a common fungal disease affecting cherry trees. It reduces photosynthesis, weakens plant growth and lowers fruit quality if left untreated.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small white powdery patches appear on young leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Powdery growth spreads across leaves and shoots causing curling.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves become distorted, dry and drop prematurely. Fruit quality declines.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms generally develop within 7–14 days after infection.

Recommended_Actions: Apply preventive fungicides before disease spreads.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Environment: Cool to moderate climate (15–25°C), fertile well-drained soil, adequate sunlight and balanced irrigation.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Description: The uploaded cherry leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest infestation. The plant appears healthy and capable of normal growth and fruit production.

Age_Cycle.Estimated: Continuous healthy growth throughout the growing season.

Organic_Treatment: Apply balanced organic fertilizers when required.
